key_insight: The paper introduces an unfitted hybrid high-order method that accurately simulates elastic waves across an imperfect interface without aligning the mesh to the interface.
engineering_relevance: It enables robust, high-order elastodynamics simulations for composite or discontinuous media where interface geometry is complex or evolving.
method: Uses a cut-cell HHO discretization with doubled unknowns in interface cells and cell agglomeration to handle tiny cuts.
Reconstructs local symmetric strain on each subcell using an interface-aware regularized stiffness matrix.
Adds interface stabilization and combines the semi-discrete scheme with Newmark or high-order SDIRK time integration.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports optimal convergence in 2D tests for k=1,2,3, robustness over sixteen orders of magnitude in compliancy, and correct wave propagation across an unresolved slipping interface.
watch_item: The method is mathematically and numerically robust, but implementation is more complex because cut-cell agglomeration and interface-aware stabilization must be handled carefully.
paper_title: An Unfitted Hybrid High-Order Method for the Elastodynamics Problem with Imperfect Interface
